newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - OCT 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Financing the Greek Armed Forces' five-year three billion drachma armaments programme was the focus of talks yesterday between Prime Minister Costas Simitis, Defence Minister Akis Tsohadzopoulos and National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou. Funds will not cover all the armaments so the shopping list must be trimmed but 40 F-16s, 50 two-seater F-16Bs, 18 Patriot missiles, new Apache combat helicopters, four frigates and four submarines as well as the upgrading of F-4 planes are all still on the list.

--Ruling party PASOK's internal dissenters reared their heads in Parliament yesterday, supporting a candidate other than that chosen by the party for a parliamentary committee. --Main opposition New Democracy to decide today on when the fourth party congress will be held. Today's meeting is expected to be tense, in light of the continuing struggle by leader Miltiades Evert to assert his position.

--Simitis requests the agreement of his party on his economic choices for 1997. The opposition the new harsh economic measures is expected to provoke forces the prime minister to ensure support from ruling party PASOK by taking the budget to party and government bodies for discussion. --Dimitra Liani, the widow of the late PASOK founder and president Andreas Papandreou, reacts strongly against the government's move to cut back her bodyguard force from 32 to six men. The government says the drastic cutbacks began some time ago and are not directed exclusively at Liani. --The new governor of the monastic community of Mount Athos, publisher Stavros Psyharis, is enthroned today, amidst the furore that has erupted over his appointment.

--The government is now discussing how deeply to cut into the incomes of the affluent, as well as establishing 'special funds' for health, education and 'social solidarity'. --A rowdy meeting at the Athens municipality finally decides on the establishment of another 5,000 new parking meters in five inner city districts.

--The inner cabinet accepts Development Minister Vasso Papandreou and Environment Minister Costas Laliotis's proposal for a revival of the tax on real estate. The final approval was given by Simitis at his evening meeting with Papandoniou. The tax is "cloaked in social garb", and aims to bolster low pensions and the government's leftist profile. --Development Minister Vasso Papandreou calls a 'mini-cabinet' meeting for today to discuss tourism-related issues. Nine ministers will attend the meeting.
--Two new taxes on real estate and businesses for the haves and have-nots. Economic ministers get the green light yesterday.
